Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. # video-use Repository Summary

**What It Is:**
video-use is an open-source video editing skill for AI coding agents like Claude Code. It automates editing tasks including removing filler words, color grading, adding subtitles and animation overlays, and self-evaluating output quality.

**Key Dependencies:**
- FFmpeg (required)
- Python packages (via uv or pip)
- ElevenLabs API (for audio transcription and speaker diarization)
- yt-dlp (optional, for downloading online sources)

**Installation Method:**
The repo provides automated setup via agent prompt or manual installation. The setup prompt instructs: `"Set up https://github.com/browser-use/video-use for me"` after reading installation documentation.

**Manual Installation Commands:**
```
git clone https://github.com/browser-use/video-use ~/Developer/video-use
ln -sfn ~/Developer/video-use ~/.claude/skills/video-use
cd ~/Developer/video-use
uv sync
brew install ffmpeg
cp .env.example .env
```

**Platform Requirements:**
The README does not explicitly specify OS or Python version requirements. It indicates macOS compatibility (via Homebrew commands) but doesn't list minimum versions for any platform or dependency.

# Caveman: Token Compression for AI Agents

## What It Is
Caveman is a skill/plugin for Claude Code and 30+ other AI coding agents that reduces output tokens by approximately 65% through terse, caveman-style responses while preserving technical accuracy.

## Problem It Solves
AI agents produce verbose replies with filler language. Caveman addresses this by enforcing brief, substance-focused output—shrinking context usage and costs without sacrificing code correctness or command precision.

## Installation
The universal installer supports macOS, Linux, Windows, and WSL:

**macOS/Linux/WSL:**
```
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/main/install.sh | bash
```

**Windows PowerShell:**
```
irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/main/install.ps1 | iex
```

For Claude Code specifically: `claude plugin marketplace add JuliusBrussee/caveman && claude plugin install caveman@caveman`

## Usage
Activate with `/caveman` or say `"talk like caveman"`. Turn off with `"normal mode"`. Six compression levels exist (lite, full, ultra, wenyan), selectable via `/caveman [level]`.

## Mechanisms
The skill operates through prompt injection rather than model fine-tuning. It instructs agents to:
- Drop rhetorical padding while preserving code, commands, and error messages byte-for-byte
- Use sentence fragments and terse phrasing
- Focus on "why" over explanatory scaffolding

Supporting commands include `/caveman-stats` (token tracking), `/caveman-compress` (rewrites memory files for persistent savings), and `/caveman-commit` (brief commit messages).

# Superpowers: Agentic Skills Framework Summary

## What It Is
Superpowers is a complete software development methodology for coding agents, combining composable skills with initial instructions to guide agent behavior systematically through design, planning, and implementation phases.

## What It Installs
The framework provides:
- **Skills library**: test-driven-development, systematic-debugging, brainstorming, writing-plans, subagent-driven-development, requesting-code-review, and others
- **Subagent orchestration**: dispatches fresh subagents per task with two-stage review
- **Git integration hooks**: uses worktrees for parallel development branches

## Core Workflows
The basic workflow progresses through seven stages: brainstorming (design refinement), using-git-worktrees (isolated workspace), writing-plans (bite-sized tasks), subagent-driven-development (fresh agents per task), test-driven-development (RED-GREEN-REFACTOR), requesting-code-review (plan compliance), and finishing-a-development-branch (merge decisions).

## Claude Code Integration
For Claude Code, install via:
```
/plugin install superpowers@claude-plugins-official
```
Or from the Superpowers marketplace:
```
/plugin marketplace add obra/superpowers-marketplace
/plugin install superpowers@superpowers-marketplace
```

## Destructive Rewrite Prevention
The README does not explicitly address preventing destructive rewrites or bug overwrites. However, the two-stage review process (spec compliance, then code quality) and systematic RED-GREEN-REFACTOR testing methodology provide safeguards through structured verification before progress.

# ECC Repository Summary

## What It Is

ECC (Everything Claude Code) is a comprehensive agent harness operating system designed for Claude Code and cross-platform AI development environments. According to the documentation, it's "The harness-native operator system for agentic work. Built from real-world multi-harness engineering workflows."

## What Gets Installed

The plugin distributes four primary components:

1. **Skills** (278 total) — Workflow definitions covering domains like TDD, security review, frontend/backend patterns, ML operations, and framework-specific development (Django, Spring Boot, Laravel, etc.)

2. **Agents** (67 total) — Specialized subagents for delegated tasks such as code review, architecture design, build error resolution, and language-specific assistance (Go, Python, Rust, TypeScript, Java, Kotlin)

3. **Hooks** (15+ event types) — Trigger-based automations that fire on SessionStart, file edits, tool use, and shell execution for context management and security checks

4. **Rules** (34 total) — Always-follow guidelines organized into `common/` (language-agnostic) and language-specific directories (TypeScript, Python, Go, Swift, PHP)

## Positioning vs. Other Frameworks

The README does not explicitly compare ECC to frameworks like ruflo/claude-flow or swarm orchestrators. However, it positions itself as production-ready infrastructure evolved from "10+ months of intensive daily use," emphasizing security hardening (AgentShield with 1282 tests), memory persistence across sessions, and cross-harness compatibility beyond Claude Code alone (Cursor, Codex, OpenCode, Gemini).

## Installation Method

The primary install path uses Claude Code's plugin marketplace:

```
/plugin marketplace add https://github.com/affaan-m/ECC
/plugin install ecc@ecc
```

For rules (which plugins cannot distribute automatically), users must manually copy language directories: `"mkdir -p ~/.claude/rules/ecc && cp -R rules/common ~/.claude/rules/ecc/"` and optionally add language-specific rule packs.

A fallback full installer exists: `"./install.sh --profile full"` for environments preferring manual control.

content.text:
## Phase 1 — Local Setup Audit

**Environment:** Node v24.14.0 / npm 11.9.0, Python 3.11.9, git 2.53.0, **ffmpeg not found**.
Global npm: `@google/gemini-cli@0.50.0`, `ruflo@3.25.2`, `ui-ux-pro-max-cli@2.10.2`.

**`~/.claude/` structure:** `CLAUDE.md`, `settings.json`, `rules/ecc/{common,python,react,typescript,web}`, `skills/{design-motion-principles, design-taste-frontend, full-output-enforcement, gpt-taste, high-end-visual-design, redesign-existing-projects, learned}`, `plugins/` (cache + marketplaces), `session-data/`, `projects/<hash>/memory/`, `.credentials.json`, `history.jsonl`.

**Plugins enabled:** `ecc@ecc`, `ui-ux-pro-max`, `impeccable`, `frontend-design`, `document-skills`. **`ruflo-core@ruflo` is set to `false`.**

⚠️ **New finding, not in memory:** `ruflo-core@ruflo` is disabled as a *plugin*, but `ruflo` is still registered as a **standalone MCP server** in `~/.claude.json` (I can see all ~300 `mcp__ruflo__*` tool names in this very session's deferred-tool list). The plugin toggle didn't kill the MCP entry — that's why the swarm/agentdb/wasm tool bloat you thought you'd turned off is still silently present. If you want the token/clutter savings you intended when you made that call, this MCP server needs to be removed too (I haven't touched it — flagging for your OK).

---

### Repo verdicts

| Repo | Verdict | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **obra/superpowers** | **Skip** | Its whole pitch — brainstorm → git-worktree isolation → bite-sized plan → fresh subagent per task → TDD → two-stage review → merge — is already what your `development-workflow.md` rule + ECC's `orch-add-feature/orch-fix-defect/orch-refine-code` skills do, and worktree isolation is already native here (`EnterWorktree`/`ExitWorktree` tools exist in this harness). Installing it duplicates a lane you already have, doesn't add a distinct "no more overwrite bugs" mechanism beyond what gated commits + code-reviewer already give you. |
| **JuliusBrussee/caveman** | **Skip** | It's a prompt-injected "talk tersely" persona (~65% token cut on prose). It directly conflicts with `full-output-enforcement`, a skill you already have installed (bans truncation/placeholders). Running both means skill-routing fights itself. Also stylistically at odds with the Luna persona you set up (natural-language collaboration, not caveman-speak). Marginal savings, real friction. |
| **browser-use/video-use** | **Not yet** | Needs `ffmpeg` (missing here) and an ElevenLabs API key; README setup commands are Homebrew-flavored (Mac-first), you're on Windows. More importantly it overlaps with skills you already have (`ecc:video-editing`, `ecc:remotion-video-creation`, `ecc:manim-video`, `ecc:videodb`) — and your own memory has a **pending Remotion install** follow-up already queued. Finish that thread before adding a third video pipeline. |
| **affaan-m/ECC** | **Confirmed keep** | Already installed, matches your lean-solo-dev call from 2026-07-09: node-native hooks (work on Windows, unlike ruflo's POSIX-only ones), 278 skills / 67 agents / 34 rules, cross-harness. This decision was already made — see `[[ecc-vs-ruflo-decision]]` in memory. Nothing here changes that; only the leftover MCP registration above is new. |

**Net effect on Phase 1's premise:** none of the three new repos meaningfully solve "prevent rewrite/bug-overwrite issues" better than what's already in your rules (`security.md`, `code-review.md`) plus normal git-diff review discipline. Adding them would be bloat relative to your stated philosophy, not upgrade.

---

## Phase 2 — Migration Strategy (Work PC → Home PC)

**No commands executed** — this is the inventory + a proposed script for your review, per your rule 1.

### Where everything lives
| What | Path |
|---|---|
| Global CLAUDE.md, rules, skills, plugins, sessions, memory | `C:\Users\mmazur\.claude\` |
| MCP server registrations, `mcpServers` config | `C:\Users\mmazur\.claude.json` |
| Auth/session token | `C:\Users\mmazur\.claude\.credentials.json` — **sensitive, handle separately, don't blindly zip-and-copy** |
| Statusline script | `C:\Users\mmazur\.claude\helpers\luna-statusline.cjs` |
| Global npm CLIs | `%APPDATA%\npm\node_modules\{@google/gemini-cli, ruflo, ui-ux-pro-max-cli}` — reinstall via `npm i -g`, don't copy (arch/path-specific) |
| Per-project memory (this session's, keyed by cwd path) | `C:\Users\mmazur\.claude\projects\C--Users-mmazur--local-bin\memory\` |

### Proposed packaging command (PowerShell, for your review — not run)

```powershell
# Excludes plugin cache (reinstallable from marketplaces) and credentials (moved separately)
$dest = "$env:USERPROFILE\claude-migration-$(Get-Date -Format yyyyMMdd).zip"
$staging = "$env:TEMP\claude-migration-staging"
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force $staging | Out-Null
robocopy "$env:USERPROFILE\.claude" "$staging\.claude" /E /XD "$env:USERPROFILE\.claude\plugins\cache" /XF ".credentials.json"
Copy-Item "$env:USERPROFILE\.claude.json" "$staging\.claude.json"
Compress-Archive -Path "$staging\*" -DestinationPath $dest -Force
```

`.credentials.json` is deliberately excluded — recommend re-authenticating (`claude login`, or however your setup handles it) on the home PC rather than copying a live token across machines.

### Restore & Sync Checklist (home PC)
1. Install Claude Code CLI + Node 24 + Python 3.11 + git first.
2. Extract archive → merge `.claude\` folder into `%USERPROFILE%\.claude\` (don't overwrite `.credentials.json` if one already exists there).
3. Merge `.claude.json` — check for `mcpServers` conflicts if the home PC already has its own MCP entries.
4. Re-run plugin installs to rebuild `plugins/cache/` (skipped in the archive on purpose):
   `/plugin marketplace add https://github.com/affaan-m/ECC` → `/plugin install ecc@ecc`, plus `ui-ux-pro-max`, `impeccable`, `frontend-design`, `document-skills`.
5. `npm i -g @google/gemini-cli ui-ux-pro-max-cli` (skip `ruflo` unless you actually want it — see finding above).
6. Verify `settings.json` → `enabledPlugins.ruflo-core@ruflo` is `false`, and check `.claude.json` for a stray `ruflo` MCP entry same as found here.
7. Confirm `~/.claude/projects/<hash>/memory/` — note the hash is derived from working-directory path; if you use a different folder path on the home PC, memory won't auto-resolve there and you'd need to copy it under the new path's hash.
8. Sanity check: open a session, confirm statusline renders (`luna-statusline.cjs` path is absolute — no edit needed since both are `C:\Users\mmazur\...` if same username).

Want me to go ahead and remove the leftover `ruflo` MCP registration from `~/.claude.json` now, since that's a concrete, low-risk cleanup that actually completes your prior decision?

input.command:
$staging = "C:\Users\mmazur\cmig"
if (Test-Path $staging) { Remove-Item -Recurse -Force $staging -Confirm:$false -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force $staging | Out-Null
robocopy "$env:USERPROFILE\.claude" "$staging\.claude" /E /XD "$env:USERPROFILE\.claude\plugins\cache" /XF ".credentials.json" /NFL /NDL /NJH
Copy-Item "$env:USERPROFILE\.claude.json" "$staging\.claude.json"
Write-Output "---staging rebuilt at short path---"
input.description: Rebuild staging directory at a short path to avoid MAX_PATH issues
